A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Manifold Steering study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, activation analyses, steering ablations, transfer experiments and latency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds layer-selection experiments on MATH500 in Appendix D, Tables 2–5.

M1.justification: Difference-in-means direction extraction, PCA projection, normalization and all-layer activation intervention remain unchanged. The added main-text explanations of prompt/response inputs and all-layer application repeat information already present in v1 Appendix A and Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same calibration data and mathematical, coding, knowledge-QA and refusal evaluations, including OpenMathInstruct-2, LiveCodeBench, GPQA-Diamond and AdvBench. The new layer analysis reuses MATH500 without adding a task, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: The mathematical and latency comparisons retain Vanilla/Original, Dynasor and SEAL. Direct-steering and refusal-direction comparisons also retain their baselines. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds an evaluation varying layer choice across the four existing LRMs on MATH500. The original selected layers, intervention strengths, sampling settings, token limits and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the addition does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests how layer choice affects the accuracy–token tradeoff across four model sizes. This targeted ablation supplements the retained intervention-strength sweeps, directional case study and other analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five responses per source question for dataset construction. Neither introduces benchmark repetition counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added layer tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 add layer-specific results. For example, v2 Table 3 reports R1-7B at layer 25 achieving 72.2% accuracy with 1,070 tokens; the selected layer 27 retains 88.4% and 2,239 tokens, already reported in v1. Existing benchmark, transfer, strength-sweep and latency results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The central theoretical justification is substantially revised. Theorem 4.1 adds a large-sample qualification, Appendix B.1 removes its high-dimensional trace-size argument, and Appendix B.2 revises noise-dominance and amplification reasoning, including deleting the reverse-triangle-inequality step and making dominance conditional. Section 4.3 replaces the P_M = I rationale with a covariance-support argument. The principal theorem conclusions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying an overthinking direction, projecting it onto a low-dimensional manifold, reducing tokens by up to 71%, preserving task performance and supporting transfer. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds an interpretation favoring the selected late layers. Revised Appendix B.2 qualifies when noise dominates and explains amplification through accumulated shifts and fresh perturbations. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning multimodal models, specialized reasoning and dynamic steering.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents the candidate-layer grids evaluated for each model, supplementing v1's selected-layer settings. Existing preprocessing, prompt templates, baseline configurations, hardware information and code-access link remain unchanged. The repeated main-text implementation explanations are not new disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of spectral filtering and probabilistic preference steering. Six additional references cover these approaches, dynamic early exit and safety-related work. The paper retains its overall positioning as mechanistic, training-free overthinking mitigation.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory edits, expands proof exposition, adds a layer-selection appendix and funding acknowledgment, and updates affiliations and publication text. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact layer-analysis tables. The existing latency table moves from Appendix D, Table 2 to Appendix E, Table 6. Existing figures and the main comparison table retain their displays, with limited surrounding layout and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The new layer ablations provide useful evidence for previously reported layer choices and reveal sensitivity that v1 did not quantify. The theoretical revision makes noise-dominance conditions more explicit, but Appendix B.2 still does not adequately justify the passage from individual perturbations to the mean-shift amplification bound in Eq. (8). The added empirical support and clarification yield a limited improvement without resolving this central theoretical weakness.
